key_insight: PCA of full-field strain measurements reveals signatures of yielding and early strain localization that are less distinguishable in instantaneous strain maps.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help identify plasticity onset and failure-prone regions in aluminum components despite thermal-exposure-induced changes in mechanical response.
method: Measure sequential strain fields during uniaxial tension using Digital Image Correlation (DIC).
Apply unsupervised Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to extract temporal deformation signatures and spatial component maps.
Compare the second-component projection peak with 0.2% offset yielding and inspect pre-transition maps for localization.
evidence_signal: For AA6063-T5 tested as received and after exposure at 100°C, 200°C, and 300°C, the second-component peak agreed with 0.2% offset yielding, while pre-transition component maps highlighted regions associated with subsequent failure.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to one alloy under uniaxial tension; robustness to other loading conditions and DIC acquisition settings remains to be established.
paper_title: Making Plasticity Visible: A Case Study for High-Temperature Exposed Aluminum Alloy
